title.narrative: Enhancing Resilience of Communities through Mine Clearance and the Improvement of the Agricultural Infrastructure (Project RECLAIM)

description.narrative: Zimbabwe’s National Development Strategy (NDS-1) emphasizes inclusive development, yet communities along the borders with Mozambique and South Africa remain affected by landmine contamination from the liberation struggle. Despite progress, around 12 square kilometres of explosive ordinance remain, hindering access to agricultural land and basic services, and posing ongoing risks to lives and livelihoods. Zimbabwe, bound by the Ottawa Convention, aims to be mine-free by 2030 following a five-year extension, though funding and capacity challenges persist. The UNDP-supported project, Enhancing Resilience of Communities through Mine Clearance and Agricultural Infrastructure, aligns with NDS-2 priorities—promoting peace, food security, and social protection. It combines mine clearance, inclusive livelihoods (via the SHEP approach), and strengthened social cohesion to empower vulnerable groups and foster climate-resilient, conflict-sensitive development. Urgent support is needed to unlock the productive potential of cleared land and ensure sustainable, inclusive growth in these underserved borderlands.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
